name: ICS/OT Network Security
description: Covers security assessment of industrial control system (ICS) and operational technology (OT) networks: Purdue model architecture review, IEC 62443 zones and conduits, IT/OT boundary and DMZ security, and OT segmentation effectiveness. Includes passive asset discovery from span ports and taps and safe, rate-limited active scanning that avoids disrupting operational processes. Protocol-level attack analysis belongs to ICSIOT-ICS-PROTO; controller assessment belongs to ICSIOT-ICS-CTRL. Supersedes NETSEC-INFRA-ICSOT.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to ICS/OT network security assessment

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands ICS/OT network architecture and why OT networks require specialised, safety-first assessment
evidence: Can explain the Purdue model levels and where the IT/OT DMZ sits
Can describe IEC 62443 zones and conduits and how they differ from flat VLAN segmentation
Knows why active scanning can crash fragile OT devices and why change control applies

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Performs basic OT network discovery and boundary review under strict supervision
evidence: Builds an asset inventory from passive traffic capture on a span port or tap in a lab ICS
Reviews IT/OT boundary firewall rule sets against a documented zone model with guidance
Runs pre-approved, rate-limited active discovery against lab OT devices
Documents findings with the operational constraints and test windows that applied

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses OT network architecture and segmentation with appropriate safety controls
evidence: Maps the as-built network to the Purdue model and documents deviations, dual-homed hosts and uncontrolled conduits
Evaluates zone and conduit enforcement, remote access paths and the IT/OT DMZ for effectiveness
Plans and executes a safe active scanning profile agreed with asset owners, including abort criteria
Produces an OT network assessment report with safety-aware, prioritised segmentation recommendations

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Assesses complex, multi-site OT networks; develops safe assessment procedures; mentors others
evidence: Assesses OT networks across sectors (energy, water, manufacturing) with differing protocols and constraints
Develops and validates passive-first discovery and safe active scanning procedures for production plants
Evaluates OT network monitoring coverage (sensor placement, protocol visibility) as part of the assessment
Mentors junior staff on OT network assessment and coordination with operations

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines the lab's OT network assessment methodology; publishes research; trains teams
evidence: Authored the lab's ICS/OT network security assessment methodology and rules of engagement
Published research or guidance on OT network architecture, segmentation or safe discovery
Recognised authority consulted on IT/OT convergence and remote-access architectures
Trains teams on ICS/OT network security assessment and safe testing practice

assessment_methods.description: In a lab ICS with simulated process, build an asset inventory from passive capture, compare it to the documented zone model, and perform an agreed safe active scan without tripping the process or devices
Review an OT network assessment report for Purdue/zone mapping accuracy, documented safety controls during testing, and actionable segmentation recommendations

equipment: ICS/SCADA lab environment with representative PLCs and HMIs
